_about: Locals' requests (scripts/empire.gd; Alex, 2026-11-15): once a local likes her enough they ask for a particular sweater and pay well over the going price for it. One at a time: the first in this list that isn't filled and whose villager has at least 'hearts' hearts. id: kept in the save once filled. who: the villager. Either fibre: an id in data/wildlife.json 'fibres' (a sweater knitted with it), or rarity: 1..5 (any sweater in her bag at least that good: 2 Uncommon, 3 Rare, 4 Epic, 5 Legendary). pay: coins on handing it over (a tenth more for each grade the sweater is above the least asked for). ask: what they say when she asks; thanks: what they say when she brings it. every_days: days after one is filled before the next local asks. Requests start once Act 1 is done. Every line and price is a draft until Alex approves it.

requests.ask: The shop's cold first thing. Could you knit me something warm? Nothing fancy, just better than the usual. Uncommon or better, as Rosa would say.
requests.thanks: That's the stuff. Warm hands, steady saw.

requests.ask: Would you make me a sweater? A proper one, by you. I'd pay, of course! Something a bit nicer than plain.
requests.thanks: I love it. I'm telling everyone you made it.

requests.ask: My round's no place for thin wool. Knit me a good one, love. Rare or better, something that'll last.
requests.thanks: Oh, that's a proper sweater. The rain can do its worst.

requests.ask: Cara, I want a sweater for Sunday. Not for the ovens, for the piazza! Something fine. Rare, at least.
requests.thanks: Look at me. Bellissimo. Sunday will be jealous of itself.

requests.ask: The terrace is freezing by four. Could you knit me something soft? Rabbit soft. Angora, if you can find any. I'll pay properly.
requests.thanks: Oh. Oh, that's soft. I'm never taking it off. Don't tell anyone I said that.

requests.ask: Nine o'clock round, every day, in all weathers. I want a sweater that can take it. They say raccoon fluff wears like iron. They're round the edge of town at dusk, the little bandits.
requests.thanks: That'll see me through the winter round. You're a marvel, Nora.

requests.ask: My dad had a fox-wool sweater. Rust red. Lasted thirty years. There are foxes up in the north woods. Knit me one like it and name your price. Well. A fair price.
requests.thanks: Just like his. Hm. Dusty in here today.

requests.ask: The ovens are hot but the mornings, the mornings are cruel! A baker needs beaver down, everybody knows this. They live in the swamp to the west. You are brave, yes?
requests.thanks: Bellissimo! Warm as fresh bread. Take a croissant too, I insist.

requests.ask: I've always wanted a mink sweater. Is that silly? I saw one in a magazine once. There are mink in the swamp and down by the beach, but they're so quick. Your dog might manage it.
requests.thanks: It's even better than the magazine. I'm going to wear it to everything.

requests.ask: Coyotes in the low foothills have been at my fence. Don't hurt them. But if you could comb one, I'd wear the proof. A farmer likes a story to tell.
requests.thanks: Ha! Now they'll know who's boss. Warm, too.

requests.ask: Forty years I've sold wool, love, and I've never once held sable. They say there's a pair in the far east meadows. Knit me one sweater of it before I retire and I'll pay you like a queen.
requests.thanks: Sable. Real sable. Oh, feel that. You've a gift, love, you really have.

requests.ask: A man in my position needs to look the part. Lynx. Up in the foothills. Nobody in three counties has a lynx sweater. I want to be the one who does.
requests.thanks: Magnificent. I look expensive, don't I? I do. Pleasure doing business.

requests.ask: There's one wild chinchilla left, up by the mountains. I've seen it twice in my life. If you ever get close enough to comb it, I'd give a lot for a sweater of it. Mostly I just want to know someone found it.
requests.thanks: You found it. You actually found it. I'll look after this for the rest of my life.
